In detail

The one specific finding for Valderrivas is a report of a man seriously wounded after being shot in a garage, sourced from a local community-news site without a clear recent date; given the uncertainty around timing and that this appears to be an isolated incident rather than a repeated pattern, it is treated as a moderate, night-time-only caution rather than a chronic concern. Other coverage found for Valderrivas concerns the Portland Valderrivas cement company (unrelated) and a cultural-heritage association, not personal safety. Sources checked: todovicalvaro.es 'Sucesos' page (garage shooting, date unclear); ABC, 29 Sept 2024 (cultural-heritage feature, non-safety).

Is Valderrivas safe?

Wandroz currently rates Valderrivas in Madrid as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Madrid during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Madrid at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Is Valderrivas safe at night?

At night, Valderrivas is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Madrid. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Valderrivas's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Madrid) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
